# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The LORD's Messiah — Blessed Are Those Born in Those Days

---

**18:1** O LORD, thy mercy is over the works of thy hands forever;
thy goodness [is] over Israel with a rich gift.

**18:2** Thine eyes are looking over them, and not one of them is in want;
thine ears are listening to the hopeful prayer of the poor.

**18:3** Thy judgments are over the whole earth in mercy;
and thy love is over the seed of Abraham, the children of Israel.

**18:4** Thy chastisement is upon us as [upon] a firstborn son,
the only-born, to turn [us] back from the obedient soul in ignorance.

**18:5** May God cleanse Israel for the day of mercy and blessing,
for the day of election when he brings back his anointed.

**18:6** Blessed are those who shall be in those days,
to see the good things of the LORD
which he shall do for the coming generation;

**18:7** under the rod of chastening of the LORD's anointed,
in the fear of his God,
in the spirit of wisdom and righteousness and strength;

**18:8** to direct every man in the works of righteousness by the fear of God,
to establish them all before the LORD;

**18:9** a good generation living in the fear of God,
in the days of mercy.

**18:10** Great is our God and glorious,
dwelling in the highest;

**18:11** who has ordered the lights [of heaven] in their courses
for the marking of times from year to year,

**18:12** and they have not deviated from the way which he appointed them;
they run their course in the fear of God every day.

**18:13** From the day when God created them forever;
and they have not gone astray since he created them
in the generations of old.

**18:14** They have not deviated from their way except when God has commanded them
by the command of his servants.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). Psalm 18 forms the closing doxology of the collection. Vv.5-9 are a deliberate refrain parallel to Ps 5 and Ps 17. The 'LORD's anointed' (v.5) and 'spirit of wisdom and righteousness and strength' (v.7) echo the messianic portrait of Ps 17 and Isa 11.*
